_comment_IMAGE_BACKBONE: Changing this requires retraining from scratch.
_comment_TEXT_ENCODER: Any valid HuggingFace model identifier is accepted.
_comment_TEXT_POOLING: How to pool transformer token representations into a single vector.
Weight each token by its average self-attention score from the
encoder's final layer, then take a weighted sum.
Tokens the model already focuses on (keywords, prices, brand names)
contribute more. Padding tokens get near-zero weight automatically.
No extra parameters - uses the encoder's own learned attention.
Better than CLS for most tasks. Slight noise from low-importance tokens.
Fast. Standard for BERT sentence classification.
Issue 7 fix: attention_weighted pooling implemented and set as default.
_comment_FUSION_TYPE: How to fuse visual and text features. Options:
attention : RECOMMENDED - full bidirectional cross-modal MHA.
Visual attends to text AND text attends to visual.
Both modalities keep their native dimensions until fusion.
concat    : concatenate native vectors -> Linear(v_dim+t_dim, HIDDEN_DIM).
Simple and fast, no attention parameters.
Change this key only - no code changes needed.
_comment_HIDDEN_DIM: Output dimension of the shared FC and all classification heads.
This is NOT the dimension of the visual or text encoders - those
keep their native dimensions (e.g. 2048 for ResNet-50, 768 for BERT).
The projection to HIDDEN_DIM happens AFTER cross-modal attention,
so no information is discarded before the modalities interact.
_comment_ATTENTION_DIM: Internal Q/K/V dimension for cross-modal attention.
Both visual (e.g. 2048) and text (e.g. 768) are projected to this
dimension before multi-head attention is computed.
768 = native DistilBERT/BERT dimension, so text is not compressed at all.
Visual (2048->768) is still compressed but unavoidable.
If you switch to bert-large (native_dim=1024), set ATTENTION_DIM=1024.
Rule of thumb: ATTENTION_DIM >= text encoder native_dim.
_comment_ATTENTION_HEADS: Number of attention heads in cross-modal MHA.
Must divide ATTENTION_DIM evenly: ATTENTION_DIM % ATTENTION_HEADS == 0.
Each head operates on ATTENTION_DIM / ATTENTION_HEADS = 64 dims.
_comment_NOISY_ATTRIBUTES: These attributes use a separate low-capacity MLP branch (noisy_branch) that is detached from the main shared representation. This prevents their noisy gradients from corrupting the features used by semantic heads. target_audience added — 28% train accuracy on a 6-class task indicates near-random labels, so it gets the same noisy-branch treatment.
_comment_NOISY_BRANCH_HIDDEN: Hidden dimension of the noisy attribute MLP branch. Smaller than HIDDEN_DIM (512) to limit capacity and prevent overfitting to noise.
_comment_USE_GRAPH_HEADS: If true, replaces independent per-attribute heads with an
AttributeCooccurrenceGraph — a GNN over attribute nodes that
propagates information between correlated attributes via learned
self-attention. A label co-occurrence prior (NMI) is used as an
attention bias so that semantic heads (theme, emotion, etc.)
share signal with noisy heads (attention_score, predicted_ctr, etc.).
Set to true to allow noisy heads to borrow signal from semantic ones.

GRAPH_HEADS._comment_D_NODE: Dimension of each attribute node's embedding.
GRAPH_HEADS._comment_N_HEADS: Number of attention heads per layer. Must divide D_NODE.

_comment_DROPOUT: Reduced from 0.5 → 0.3. SAM provides complementary flat-minima regularisation, so explicit dropout can be loosened to let more signal flow through the GNN heads.
_comment_FREEZE_BACKBONE: Freeze the pretrained visual backbone convolutional weights.
With 4860 training samples and ResNet-18 (11M params),
the backbone memorises training images (val loss plateaued at ep5).
Freezing forces the model to use general ImageNet features which
generalise far better on small datasets.
The cross-modal attention, shared FC, and all heads remain fully trainable.
Expected impact: -5% train accuracy, +3-5% val accuracy, smaller train/val gap.
_comment_DEEP_SHARED_LAYER: If true, use a two-layer shared FC after fusion:
If false, use a single layer: fusion_dim -> HIDDEN_DIM
_comment_ATTRIBUTE_LOSS_WEIGHTS: Per-attribute multiplier applied to each head's CrossEntropyLoss before summing.
be learned from image+text content (Cramér's V ≈ 0.02–0.04).
Reduced from 0.1 → 0.05 to further silence gradient noise from these heads,
letting the semantic heads (sentiment, emotion, trust_safety) dominate training.
target_audience (6 age groups) has moderate content correlation but benefits from
slightly higher weight than the noise heads, yet lower than pure semantic heads.
Used by train_epoch in train_model.py — see ATTRIBUTE_LOSS_WEIGHTS key.
_comment_STOP_GRADIENT_HEADS: Attribute heads whose gradients are detached from the shared representation.
These heads still compute forward pass (for monitoring) and their own weights
receive gradients, but their loss does NOT flow back into shared_fc or fusion.
This prevents noisy engagement metrics from corrupting the shared features that
semantic heads (sentiment, emotion, trust_safety) depend on.
predicted_ctr and likelihood_shares have Cramér's V ≈ 0.02 with content —
they are essentially random noise and their gradients harm generalisation.
_comment_image_size: Input image size as [width, height]. Must match what the backbone expects.
BUG-09 FIX: image/pipeline.py now uses this value (not a hardcoded 224).
Used by: transforms.py, pipeline.py, evaluate.py, predict_image.py, analyze_model.py
_comment_use_text: Set to false to disable the text branch entirely.
_comment_text_max_length: Maximum token sequence length for the text encoder.
Must be consistent across training, validation, and inference.
BUG-05/10 FIX: all code now reads this value from config.
Used by: pipeline.py, train_model.py script, evaluate.py, predict_image.py, tokenizer.py
_comment_DATASET_ROOT: Optional path to the dataset root for training and evaluation.
If set, the code resolves splits from this directory instead of
Use an absolute path such as the Kaggle input path.
_comment_training_note: IMPORTANT: These keys must be at the TOP LEVEL of this file.
Do NOT nest them under a 'model' key.
BUG-28 NOTE: setup_training_components reads from the top-level config.
_comment_learning_rate: LR for randomly initialised layers (heads, projection, shared FC). Reduced from 2e-4 → 1e-4: slower learning reduces overfitting on small dataset.
_comment_use_sam: If true, wraps the optimizer with Sharpness-Aware Minimization.
SAM perturbs weights toward a sharper loss region, then updates from
the original position using the gradient at the perturbed point.
This encourages flatter minima that generalise better — especially
Typically provides +2-5% accuracy at no inference cost.
_comment_sam_rho: 0.05 is the default from the SAM paper and works well with AdamW.
Large rho → stronger regularisation, may underfit.
Small rho → weaker regularisation, may overfit.
_comment_encoder_learning_rate: LR for the pretrained text encoder (text_module.encoder).
Should be ~10-25x lower than learning_rate to avoid catastrophic forgetting.
Raised from 5e-6 → 2e-5: the encoder was barely fine-tuning at 5e-6.
_comment_weight_decay: L2 regularisation applied to non-bias, non-LayerNorm parameters.
Reduced from 0.02 → 0.01: SAM's flat-minima regularisation replaces
some of the burden previously placed on explicit weight decay.
Bias and LayerNorm weights always have weight_decay=0 (standard BERT recipe).
BUG-02 FIX: no longer passed as a global AdamW arg (was redundant).
_comment_batch_size: With DataParallel (multi-GPU) each GPU processes batch_size/num_gpus samples.
Doubled from 32 → 64 to use both T4 GPUs effectively (32 samples/GPU).
Larger batches also stabilise gradient estimates with only 4860 training samples.
BUG-07 FIX: train DataLoader uses drop_last=True so the last batch
is never smaller than batch_size (prevents BatchNorm crash on batch=1).
_comment_num_workers: Number of DataLoader worker processes for data loading.
Higher values help keep multiple GPUs fed with data.
Set to 0 to load data in the main process (useful for debugging).
Capped to available CPU count at runtime.
_comment_warmup_epochs: Number of linear LR warmup epochs at the start of training.
LR ramps from near-zero to learning_rate over this many epochs.
Reduced from 15 → 5: with only 4860 samples, 15 warmup epochs means the
LR didn't peak until epoch 15, at which point val loss was already rising.
5 epochs gives stable early gradients without delaying convergence.
BUG-01 FIX: warmup is handled by SequentialLR+LinearLR in pipeline.py.
_comment_mixup_alpha: Mixup Beta distribution parameter. 0 disables Mixup.
Set to 0: multi-task training with 9 conflicting label sets makes Mixup harmful.
A mixed image of 'Food' and 'Tech' ads has no valid joint labels.
Standard image augmentation (already configured) is sufficient.
_comment_FOCAL_LOSS_GAMMA: Per-attribute gamma for Focal Loss. gamma=0 disables focal loss (uses standard CE).
All 4 noisy attrs migrated to GCELoss (below) because GCE is bounded — prevents
individual very-wrong samples from dominating the gradient.
Set to a float to apply the same gamma to all attributes, or a dict for per-attr control.
_comment_GCE_Q: Per-attribute q for Generalized Cross Entropy Loss.
GCE is bounded: max loss = 1/q (e.g. q=0.5 → max loss = 2.0).
Lower q = stronger noise robustness. q=0.0 = standard CE.
Replaced FocalLoss for noisy attrs because GCE's bounded nature
provides stronger protection against individual noisy labels without
the easy-example down-weighting that can hurt already-weak signal.
attention_score and target_audience get q=0.5 (stronger robustness),
_comment_label_smoothing: Per-attribute label smoothing. Can be a float (uniform) or a dict (per-attribute).
Reduced all noisy attrs from 0.3 → 0.1: aggressive smoothing was producing
targets like [0.233, 0.233, 0.533] for 3-class problems — too much noise for
the model to extract any signal. 0.1 gives [0.033, 0.033, 0.933] which still
provides regularisation without obliterating the weak signal.
_comment_USE_TTA: If true, applies test-time augmentation (horizontal flip averaging) during validation for ~1-3% accuracy improvement at no training cost.
_comment_ELR_BETA: Beta coefficient for Early Learning Regularization. Controls EMA momentum for per-target tracking. Typical range: 0.3–0.9.
_comment_USE_COTEACHING: If true, use Co-teaching (two models, small-loss sample exchange). Requires USE_COTEACHING=true and two optimizer configs.
_comment_COTEACHING_NOISE_RATE: Estimated label noise rate for Co-teaching. Determines what fraction of samples with the largest losses are discarded each batch.
_comment_USE_DIVIDEMIX: DivideMix: GMM-based clean/noisy split + co-training for sample-level noise robustness. Overrides USE_COTEACHING. The 4 noisy engagement attrs have near-random labels — DivideMix lets the model identify which training samples have reliable labels per-attribute and trains on them differently.
_comment_DIVIDEMIX_WARMUP_EPOCHS: Number of warmup epochs where DivideMix trains on the full dataset before applying GMM splitting.
_comment_DIVIDEMIX_CLEAN_THRESHOLD: GMM probability threshold for clean/noisy split in DivideMix.
_comment_DIVIDEMIX_LAMBDA_U: Weight for unsupervised (noisy sample) loss in DivideMix. Reduced from 25.0 → 1.0: original DivideMix designed for single-label CIFAR, but with 9 attributes the consistency CE sums to ~10-18 per sample — 25x gave 250-450 loss, overwhelming supervised signal.
_comment_LABEL_CORRECTION_ENABLED: Progressive label correction for noisy samples identified by DivideMix GMM. After GMM split, replaces noisy labels with model's argmax prediction where confidence > threshold. Fraction corrected ramps from 0 -> max_rate over ramp_epochs.
_comment_LABEL_CORRECTION_RAMP_EPOCHS: Number of divide-phase epochs to ramp correction fraction from 0 to LABEL_CORRECTION_MAX_RATE.
_comment_LABEL_CORRECTION_MAX_RATE: Max fraction of eligible noisy samples corrected per epoch. epoch 11=0%, 12=9%, 15=45%, 20=90%, 30+=90%.
_comment_LABEL_CORRECTION_CONFIDENCE_THR: Min softmax confidence to accept a label correction. Prevents low-confidence corrections from introducing noise.
_comment_FIXMATCH_ENABLED: FixMatch-style consistency on noisy-set samples. Strong-aug forward pass, CE against same-model weak-aug pseudo-label gated by confidence threshold.
_comment_FIXMATCH_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: Min pseudo-label confidence for FixMatch loss. Only applies where weak-aug max(softmax) > this value.
_comment_FIXMATCH_LOSS_WEIGHT: Weight for FixMatch loss. 1.0 = same scale as supervised CE.
_comment_SIMCLR_PRETRAIN: If true, run SimCLR self-supervised pre-training before supervised training.
_comment_SIMCLR_CONFIG: Hyperparameters for SimCLR pre-training. Only used when SIMCLR_PRETRAIN=true.
_comment_USE_PROTOTYPICAL_HEADS: If true, replaces linear classification heads for NOISY_ATTRIBUTES with PrototypicalNetwork heads (cosine similarity to learnable prototypes).
_comment_USE_L2RW: If true, use Learning to Reweight (Ren et al.) — meta-learning per-sample weights from a clean validation set.
_comment_USE_META_WEIGHT_NET: If true, use Meta-Weight-Net (Shu et al.) — MLP mapping per-sample loss to weight, trained with bi-level meta-objective.
_comment_N_CO_TRAIN_MODELS: Number of co-training models for DivideMix/MultiModelCoTrain. 2 = standard DivideMix. 3+ = majority-vote ensemble.
_comment_USE_CONFIDENT_LEARNING: If true, run CleanLab-style confident learning offline before each epoch to identify likely mislabeled samples.
_comment_CONFIDENT_LEARNING_THRESHOLD: Threshold for confident learning. 'auto' uses per-class thresholds from CleanLab.
_comment_USE_UDA_TEXT_AUG: If true, apply UDA-style text augmentation (back-translation or BERT masking) during training.
_comment_UDA_TEXT_AUG_CONFIG: Hyperparameters for text augmentation. method can be 'back_translate' or 'bert_mask'.
_comment_early_stopping_patience: Stop training if val accuracy does not improve for this many consecutive epochs.
Reduced from 15 → 10: with the train/val gap already opening at epoch 11,
15 patience epochs wastes compute on a diverging run.
Set to 0 to disable early stopping.
_comment_checkpoint_dir: Directory to save model checkpoints during training.
Best checkpoints are saved as best_model_epoch_N_acc_X.pt.
Last epoch checkpoint is saved as last_model.pt.
_comment_log_dir: Directory to store training logs (CSV of per-epoch metrics).
_comment_scheduler_type: LR decay schedule after warmup. Options:
cosine : CosineAnnealingLR from warmup_end to epoch N (recommended)
step   : StepLR - multiply LR by scheduler_gamma every scheduler_step_size epochs
_comment_scheduler_eta_min: Minimum LR for cosine scheduler. Only used when scheduler_type = 'cosine'.
_comment_scheduler_step_size: Decay interval in epochs. Only used when scheduler_type = 'step'.
_comment_scheduler_gamma: LR multiplier per step. Only used when scheduler_type = 'step'.
_comment_class_weights_note: BUG-25 FIX: If this key is absent, weights are auto-computed from the
training CSV using inverse-frequency: weight[i] = total / (num_classes * count[i]).
Set to {} to explicitly disable weighting.
Set to a dict of lists to use fixed weights (overrides auto-computation).
